_comment: SEC-004 unsafe allowlist. Gate: scripts/rust-port/unsafe-inventory.py (make rust-unsafe-inventory). Counts are exact `unsafe` keyword tokens (comments and literals excluded). Production (scope=src) tokens also need a // SAFETY: comment. Add an entry only with a safety invariant and a focused test.

unsafe.invariant: Only the `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` on the `#[cfg(windows)]` module declaration of index_status_process_windows.rs; it contains no unsafe token itself.

Windows-only Win32 Job Object / thread-snapshot FFI behind owning RAII handle wrappers: handles are opened/created in this module, closed exactly once on drop, structs have the SDK ABI layout, and the suspended child is resumed only after Job assignment. Every call site carries a `// SAFETY:` comment. Windows is not a required port target (scope decision 2026-10-29): the focused tests compile and run only on Windows and are NOT exercised by the macOS/Linux local gate.

Unix libc FFI only: self-pipe/fcntl/poll/signal/raise/gethostname called with valid stack buffers and descriptors created in this module; the SIGINT/SIGTERM handler `on_signal` performs only async-signal-safe operations (atomic store + one `write`). Every call site carries a `// SAFETY:` comment (enforced by the inventory).

Edition-2024 `std::env::set_var`/`remove_var` are `unsafe` because a concurrent environment read is a data race. Calls are serialised by a process-wide mutex in `with_sidecar_env`, so no test thread reads the environment concurrently.
Edition-2024 `std::env::set_var`/`remove_var` are `unsafe` because a concurrent environment read is a data race. Calls are serialised by `ENV_LOCK`.

`libc::mkfifo` receives a valid NUL-terminated `CString` path that outlives the call; it creates a FIFO inside the test's private scratch vault to prove the exporter rejects non-regular files.
`libc::signal(SIGPIPE, SIG_DFL)` only resets one signal disposition (restores Go's die-on-EPIPE behaviour); no handler is installed and no memory is shared.

Edition-2024 `std::env::set_var`/`remove_var` are `unsafe` because a concurrent environment read is a data race. The test binary runs one single-threaded `#[test]`, so the mutation is confined to it (documented at `set_env`).
